Compares; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — controlled case study: one production agent (GitHub Copilot CLI) with two models re-implements a React Fluent-UI table in Angular under three oracle-availability conditions (c0 no oracle, c3 oracle in loop with guardrail prompt, c9 oracle with looser prompt), 3 runs each (18 runs); adds a mechanical library audit confirmed by no-op ablation

No SDD approach. Agent: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.56, as shipped (per-model harness, system prompt, default tools), with claude-opus-4.7 (xhigh reasoning, 1M context) and gpt-5.5 (xhigh reasoning). Conditions differ only in AGENTS.md: c0, c3, c9. 'Code-as-spec': the specification is a runnable reference implementation (@fluentui/react-components 9.73.7, pinned commit) plus TASK.md

TASK.md (byte-identical in all runs): reference system and pinned version, target framework (Angular standalone components, signals, services, DI), goal (production-grade reusable component library), component specifications (selectors, inputs, outputs, CSS classes, behaviours), table of state features mapping React hooks to Angular services/directives. AGENTS.md (one per condition): resources, goal, 'How to work' steps, 'What good looks like'. Executable reference (React source, ~5800 LOC); in c3/c9 also the reference Storybook and the 'wild-test' oracle (names and pass/fail only)

AGENTS.md 'How to work': (1) fetch the reference source; (2) initialise the Angular project; (3) implement components, services, directives; (4) verify (c0: build and test; c3: may use wild-test as a helper; c9: run wild-test, fix failures, rerun); (5) decide when done (c0/c3: when you believe it is complete and correct; c9: when wild-test passes and the task is covered)
None: Copilot CLI in auto-approving (--yolo) mode; every run ended in a voluntary shutdown
Full workflow of the agent on one task; the agent-facing instruction file (AGENTS.md) and oracle access are varied
Not classifiable; authors' wording: 'code-as-spec', 'the reference implementation is the executable specification', TASK.md as 'the task specification'

Library audit per stateful subsystem (selection, sort, resize, grid navigation): ND (demo calls the library), L2 (library implementation exists but demo reimplements inline, library dead), L1 (no library implementation); '#disp.' = count of L1/L2 out of 4. Automatic: Playwright oracle run by the identical harness with a single worker (completeness of each scoring run verified); static audit tool (audit.py --verify, regex/AST, reproduces 48/48 oracle cells); no-op ablation of library methods; counts from delivered source; trajectory census from events.jsonl. Manual: post-hoc consumer kits authored for the six c0 runs (no demo shipped); selection of trajectory quotes

Success criterion stated by the authors: a correct re-implementation passes all 222 oracle tests, and the deliverable must be a reusable library actually used by the demo (ND, no L1/L2); no cost criterion. (1) Copilot CLI + claude-opus-4.7, c0 (no oracle), 3 runs: parity 177/165/189; #disp 0/0/0; manifest 3/3, unit tests 10/11/11, strict 3/3; ~17-27 min. Quality: partly (genuine library, 33-57 behaviours missing). Cost: no criterion stated by the authors. (2) Copilot CLI + claude-opus-4.7, c3 (oracle, guardrail prompt): 222/222/222; #disp 0/0/0. Quality: works on parity and library routing, but library craft shed (Claude oracle runs: 0/6 manifests, 0/6 unit tests, 1/6 strict). Cost: no criterion stated by the authors (Claude oracle runs 65-221 min). (3) Copilot CLI + claude-opus-4.7, c9 (oracle, looser prompt): 222/222/222; #disp 0/1/3 (R2 selection L2; R3 selection L2, sort L2, resize L1). Quality: partly (1 of 3 runs library-routed). Cost: no criterion stated by the authors. (4) Copilot CLI + gpt-5.5, c0: 148/166/173; #disp 0/0/0. Quality: partly (library present, 49-74 behaviours missing). Cost: no criterion stated by the authors. (5) Copilot CLI + gpt-5.5, c3: 221/222/161 (R3 never ran the oracle, no demo, scored post-hoc); #disp 3/3/0. Quality: does not work (two runs leave selection, sort, resize L2; the library-routed run is incomplete). Cost: no criterion stated by the authors (c3-R3 ~9 min). (6) Copilot CLI + gpt-5.5, c9: 222/221/221; #disp 3/4/3 (R2 has no library directory at all). Quality: does not work. Cost: no criterion stated by the authors
fields.why: Metric values re-checked against Tables 1-2 and Appendix J (all match). The authors state the criterion (all 222 tests pass, and the requested reusable library is what the demo actually runs, p. 2-3, 15) but give no works/partly verdict per configuration, so the verdicts are the extractor's application of that two-part criterion. Borderline: GPT c9 (parity 221-222, library dead or absent) could be read as partly rather than does not work; Claude c3 (222, all ND) as partly because manifest and unit tests were shed, though craft is not part of the stated criterion
fields.doubt: Os autores dão o critério (222 testes e biblioteca realmente usada) mas não dão veredictos. Confirma se GPT c3/c9 é 'does not work' e Claude c3 'works' apesar da perda de manifest e testes.

fields.v: Task: one (Fluent UI Table React -> Angular). Configurations: 2 models on Copilot CLI x 3 conditions. Baseline: c0 (standard benchmark convention, oracle post-hoc). Held constant: TASK.md byte-identical, AGENTS.md identical within condition across agents, container image, CLI version 1.0.56, Node runtime, empty workspace, unrestricted internet; per-model harness defaults kept as shipped (product-level comparison). Acceptance: hidden 222-test Playwright oracle, plus library audit and no-op ablation. Repetitions: 3 per (condition, model), 18 runs. Human intervention: none (--yolo). c9 changes several prompt elements at once by design

With the oracle in the loop parity reaches 221-222 (except GPT c3-R3, 161) vs 148-189 without, but the library is left dead or absent: disposition in 2/6 Claude oracle runs (only under c9) and 5/6 GPT oracle runs; grid navigation stays library-routed in 10 of 11 demo-bearing oracle runs. Claude milder than GPT. Library craft drops for Claude (manifest 3/3 -> 0/6, unit tests 10-11 -> 0/6, strict 3/3 -> 1/6). Ablation: all 12 L2 cells inert under no-op; 3 ND controls load-bearing (29 -> 17, 34 -> 19, 34 -> 27 tests). No statistical tests (claim of existence/mechanism, not prevalence)

Distinguished conditions and agents and exposed what the score alone could not (audit confirmed by ablation in 15/15 targets; audit tool 48/48). Three repetitions per cell, but outcomes varied within some cells (Claude c9 #disp 0/1/3; GPT c3 parity 221/222/161 with R3 never invoking the oracle); no variance or repeatability analysis (deliberately a mechanism claim). Limitations stated: small N, prevalence across agents, signals and model families open; c9 is a bundled edit, the load-bearing contrast is c0 vs oracle; c0 scored through manually authored consumer kits; cross-agent comparison at product level, model and harness not separated

Limitations: one controlled instance (2 agents x 3 conditions); prevalence open; cause of per-subsystem variation open; model vs harness disposition not separated. Gaps: pass-rate benchmarks cannot see whether the requested artefact was delivered or whether agents choose appropriate validation unprompted ('validation self-awareness'); future work on graded in-loop signals, a matrix across agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Aider), model tiers and artefact types, post-training effects, and a benchmark methodology combining code-as-spec, controlled oracle exposure and post-hoc audit

Abstract speaks of 'two production Copilot CLI agents' (one CLI, two models). Text cites 114 oracle invocations to Section 4, but the figure appears only in Appendix J. Appendix L refers to 'the author' (singular) while three authors are listed. GPT c3-R3 is counted among oracle runs though it never invoked the oracle and was scored post-hoc. Authors are at Microsoft, the evaluated agent is GitHub Copilot CLI and the reference is Microsoft's Fluent UI. Replication package (per-run workspaces, audit tool, ablation diffs, consumer kits, trajectory quotes) at github.com/yanuoma/b2t; no pre-registration. Programming language: TypeScript (Angular target, React reference). LLM assistance disclosed for harness code and manuscript
